daily.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
daily.summary: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

daily.title: Trump, Putin agree on deal to release Russian diesel to US, world markets
daily.summary: Russia will supply diesel to global markets in a bid to lower prices, US President Donald Trump has said. The move reverses years of pressure on the Russian economy following the invasion of Ukraine.

daily.title: Strong earthquake shakes Panama, prompting tsunami alert
daily.summary: Tremors were felt in the capital city when a powerful earthquake shook Panama, triggering a tsunami threat warning in Central and South America.

daily.title: UAE: Omani Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack
daily.summary: A Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight into the terminal at Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, according to a UAE official.

daily.title: China, EU reach deal to 'moderate' China's car exports to EU
daily.summary: An agreement between the EU and China would reduce exports of Chinese electric and plug-in hybrid cars to the 27-member European bloc by up to 50%, according to the EU trade envoy.

daily.title: Brussels: Rioters clash with police at anti-austerity rally
daily.summary: Violent rioters, many of whom were masked, confronted police at the edge of an anti-austerity march in Brussels. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas.

daily.title: Eritrean troops in Ethiopia raise fears of a regional war
daily.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea are trading blame for confrontations in Tigray amid international calls for restraint. Their respective allies have the potential to catapult the conflict into a regional war.

daily.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
daily.summary: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

daily.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
daily.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

daily.title: US imposes sanctions aiming to 'dismantle' International Criminal Court
daily.summary: The US has announced new sanctions on the International Criminal Court. It's the latest in a series of steps by the Donald Trump administration as it seeks to "dismantle" the intergovernmental organization.

daily.title: Saudi coalition vows 'firm' response after airport attack kills 3
daily.summary: Saudi Arabia and its allied forces in Yemen vowed a "firm response" to Houthi attacks that target civilians. The kingdom's authorities said three Saudi nationals were killed in Thursday's attack on Riyadh airport.

daily.title: Is China seeking to restrict Taiwan's cultural presence?
daily.summary: From coffee competitions to literature awards, Beijing appears to be working to limit Taiwan's international cultural and political impact.

daily.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
daily.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

daily.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
daily.summary: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

daily.title: India's 'cockroaches' vs Election Commission: What you need to know ahead of CJP's October 10 protests
daily.summary: The Indian capital New Delhi has been turned into a fortress with train and metro cancelations, barricades and heavy police presence ahead of Saturday's planned protests against the chief of India's electoral body.

daily.title: Hurricane Isaias intensifies en route to US Gulf Coast
daily.summary: Oil and gas production in the Gulf of Mexico has already been affected by the approaching hurricane, which has strengthened so far to Category 2.

daily.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
daily.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

daily.title: France: Investigators recover 2 stolen Renoir paintings
daily.summary: Thieves had initially taken four pieces with a value of over $10 million, but dropped two as they fled. Officials praised everyone that tracked down the paintings, but didn't reveal how they found them.

daily.title: Voting to begin in local elections in the Czech Republic
daily.summary: The vote is being seen as a test of popularity for Prime Minister Andrej Babis's government.

daily.title: South Africa pulls asylum directive after violent protests in Johannesburg, Durban
daily.summary: South Africa has withdrawn a controversial asylum directive after anti-migrant protests descended into violence and chaos on Thursday.

daily.title: Germany women's football team: Can Ena Mahmutovic make a case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper?
daily.summary: The women's friendlies against Australia and Japan present an opportunity for Ena Mahmutovic to make her case for succeeding Ann-Katrin Berger as Germany's first-choice goalkeeper.

daily.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina will soon have a new Grand Mufti
daily.summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia and Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

daily.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
daily.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

weekly.title: EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
weekly.summary: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

weekly.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
weekly.summary: The works of this year's Nobel Literature Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

weekly.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
weekly.summary: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

weekly.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
weekly.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.

weekly.title: Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
weekly.summary: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

weekly.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
weekly.summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

weekly.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
weekly.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

weekly.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
weekly.summary: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

weekly.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
weekly.summary: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

weekly.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
weekly.summary: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

weekly.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
weekly.summary: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

weekly.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
weekly.summary: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

weekly.title: 90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
weekly.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Britpop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers
weekly.summary: Political extremism threatens Germany's existing social order, Chancellor Merz has said. The Transport Ministry has proposed a five-year plan to improve Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure.

weekly.title: EU enlargement: European Commission tables reforms to prepare bloc for new members
weekly.summary: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

weekly.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
weekly.summary: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

weekly.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
weekly.summary: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."

weekly.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
weekly.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

weekly.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
weekly.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

weekly.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
weekly.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

weekly.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
weekly.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

weekly.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
weekly.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

weekly.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the campaign.

weekly.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
weekly.summary: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

weekly.title: Germany shaken by espionage and treason allegations
weekly.summary: The former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, the BND, has been accused of spying for a foreign country. Never before has a German official of August Hanning's stature been accused of treason.

weekly.title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
weekly.summary: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

weekly.title: France's conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

weekly.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
weekly.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

weekly.title: Germany's far-right AfD makes history again in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: For the first time since the end of World War II, a German state parliament has chosen parliamentary speaker from the far right: Tobias Rausch of the Alternative for Germany (AfD).

weekly.title: Nobel Literature Prize: How the winner is secretly chosen
weekly.summary: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in Literature?

weekly.title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
weekly.summary: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

weekly.title: AI models keep hacking real systems during tests. What does this mean?
weekly.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

weekly.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists
weekly.summary: At a rare public hearing Germany's intelligence agencies identified Russia as the country's most dangerous adversary. The threat from China is also coming into focus. And the homegrown far right also poses a challenge.

weekly.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament
weekly.summary: For the first time since World War II, a far-right party has a house speaker in a German state parliament. And Germany's foreign minister has warned that the climate crisis could fuel extremism.

weekly.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
weekly.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

weekly.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there
weekly.summary: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the countries.

weekly.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
weekly.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

weekly.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?
weekly.summary: Germany's top court, which turned 75 this year, is losing the population's trust, surveys show. Some say reforms in the way it picks candidates would help, to also accept candidates nominated by the far-right AfD.

weekly.title: Germany news: Spy chief warns Russia conflict risk growing
weekly.summary: Moscow is already waging a "shadow war" against Europe, the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service says. The Left Party is taking a case over remarks by the CDU's Katherina Reiche to a top court.

weekly.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
weekly.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

weekly.title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
weekly.summary: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

weekly.title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
weekly.summary: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

weekly.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
weekly.summary: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

weekly.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
weekly.summary: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

weekly.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
weekly.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

weekly.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity
weekly.summary: A new study highlights persistent structural disparities in wealth and leadership positions between East and West Germany, 36 years after reunification.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
